verified.entry_point: GET /oidc/callback and POST /saml/acs -> OidcService/SamlService -> UserProvisioningService::provisionUser (the shared provisioning sink both callbacks call; hidden tests drive it with the production OidcUserInfo/SamlUserInfo values and a real PDO connection)
sites: sql/poweradmin-mysql-db-structure.sql:343-344 and :360-361 (stored identity columns and their unique key)
routes: OIDC sign-in callback (subject + provider -> local account)
SAML ACS assertion (name identifier + provider -> local account)
OIDC link write when an account is auto-provisioned or linked by email
SAML link write when an account is auto-provisioned or linked by email
OIDC/SAML orphan-link cleanup reached from the subject lookup
services: MariaDB 10.11 server on loopback, started by the verifier before the suites run
SQLite through pdo_sqlite (in-memory) for the backend-compatibility suite

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: the sign-in path has no status-coded refusal; an exception is caught and treated as a failed sign-in, and the functional suites would fail
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: the asserted identifier is not normalised or adjusted between receipt and comparison
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: identifiers are opaque strings compared for equality; there is no parser whose spelling mismatch could hide the value
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: the decision is a stored-record match, not an authority or secret lookup that could fail open

traps.shape: stored column collation / unique key produced by the schema file, which the lookup query never reads; a distinct identity that differs by case cannot keep its own binding because the stored uniqueness treats the two subjects as equal
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the shipped MySQL schema is the product's own fresh-install definition

traps.shape: an identifier that differs from a stored one only by a trailing character that the engine's padding rules ignore; a binary collation alone still compares the two as equal
traps.where: lib/Application/Service/UserProvisioningService.php:147 and :424 (subject/provider comparison in both protocol lookups)
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the padded comparison is exactly what the reported lookup does

traps.shape: an installation whose identity columns were created with a character set other than the one a fixed query names; the comparison clause is invalid there and the lookup error is swallowed, so every sign-in silently becomes a new account

traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the installer offers latin1 collations and the shipped defaults still use latin1
